status: Performance. 189 ± 62 per game over 3 seeds (185, 166 and 215; 95% interval), with 0.2–3.9% deaths. The exact-belief heuristic earns 573 and knowing the layout is worth 936. About 70% of the agent's games end unfinished after 50 steps, against 29% for the heuristic. The agent rarely dies, but it often fails to find the gold in time.

Interpretability. The latent is organised first by the percept just received. A probe recovers the hunter's cell and heading 55–58% and 55–60% of the time on random-action histories, and 83–88% and 87–90% on the agent's own games. The same network trained on exact targets reaches 99.9% and 100%. The hazard beliefs beat a constant guess, but they stay coarse.

Training. The belief filter and the observation model train jointly, and they overfit when they train too many times per game. 64 gradient updates per 64 new games, uniform random actions mixed into collection (ε from 0.25 down to 0.1) and storing the greedy evaluation games keep the death model calibrated on fresh games. Weight decay did not help, and the network architecture was never the limit.

Next. Close the unfinished-game gap: a value scale fitted to the game's ±1000 rewards, longer training at the same update rate, and measuring how much of the remaining gap the latent's coarse belief explains.
